text: The night was dark, the darkest of the year.
Sunny found a cave behind the ferns.
“Hello?” she whispered into the dark.
And then — a tiny light blinked on above.
Then two, then ten, then hundreds, soft and blue,
like all the stars had come inside to sleep.
Glow worms! Painting starlight on the stone,
a sky of tiny lanterns in the cave.
“Hello,” they twinkled. “Welcome to our sky.
We keep the dark all soft and full of light.”
Sunny lay upon the mossy floor,
and watched the living stars above her glow.
“Are you ever scared of the dark?” she asked.
“Oh no,” they glowed. “The dark is where we shine.”
And Sunny smiled, because she understood:
the dark is just a home for gentle lights.
One by one the glow worms dimmed their lamps,
the way the stars grow soft before the dawn.
A few stayed glowing, keeping gentle watch,
tiny nightlights for the sleeping cave.
Sunny nestled deep into the moss,
beneath the softest starlight ever made.
The cave was still. The lights hummed low and blue.
Everything was peaceful, calm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy under glowing stars.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath a starlit ceiling,
never once afraid of the gentle dark.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little glow worms.
Goodnight, starry cave. Goodnight, little one.
